[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SCP-2.7.16.md#abb-context]

### ABB Context

- **Parent L2 Capability**: Container Orchestration Security — [GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02](../GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02.md)
- **ABB Catalog**: [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06](../GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06.md)
- **Capability Statement**: The enterprise SHALL have an architectural capability to protect the integrity of the container orchestration control plane — the components that make scheduling, routing, and configuration decisions for the entire workload fleet.
page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SCP-2.7.16.md#abb-scope]

### ABB Scope

**In Scope**:
- Architectural capability to protect orchestration control plane components from unauthorized access and configuration manipulation
- Secure communication between control plane components
- Audit logging of all control plane operations
- Encryption of sensitive state stored by the control plane

**Out of Scope**:
- RBAC and admission control for workload deployments (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SRBAC-2.7.15)
- Host/node OS security (see Cloud & Infrastructure Security domain)
- Network policy for pod-to-pod communication (see Network Security domain)
- Security controls, tool selection, or configuration baselines (`standards/security/`)

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SCP-2.7.16.md#core-principles]

### Core Principles

- The control plane API endpoint SHALL be accessible only through authenticated, authorized channels — unauthenticated access SHALL NOT be permitted.
- All communication between control plane components SHALL be mutually authenticated and encrypted in transit.
- Control plane state SHALL be encrypted at rest.
- All control plane operations SHALL produce an immutable audit log that is forwarded to the security monitoring capability.
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SCP-2.7.16.md#api-server-access-control]

#### API Server Access Control

**Architectural intent**: Ensure the orchestration platform's primary management interface is protected from unauthorized access.

**Design guidance**:
- The API server SHALL enforce mutual TLS for all inter-component communication.
- Anonymous access to the API server SHALL be disabled.
- The API server SHALL be network-isolated from workload networks; management access SHALL require explicit routing through a defined administrative path.
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SCP-2.7.16.md#state-integrity]

#### State Integrity

**Architectural intent**: Protect the configuration and state data that the control plane uses to make scheduling and routing decisions.

**Design guidance**:
- State storage (e.g., the distributed key-value store) SHALL be encrypted at rest using keys managed through the Secrets Vault ABB (GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-VAULT-2.7.21).
- Access to state storage SHALL be restricted to control plane components only; direct external access SHALL NOT be permitted.
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SCP-2.7.16.md#control-plane-audit]

#### Control Plane Audit

**Architectural intent**: Maintain a complete, tamper-evident record of all control plane operations for detection and forensics.

**Design guidance**:
- Audit logging SHALL capture all API server requests including the requesting identity, resource, verb, and response code.
- Audit logs SHALL be forwarded to the SecOps monitoring capability and SHALL NOT be stored only on the cluster.
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SCP-2.7.16.md#integration-interfaces]

### Integration Interfaces

| Interface | Direction | Consuming ABB | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Administrative Access | Inbound | Platform Engineering | Authenticated management access to control plane API |
| State Storage | Bidirectional | Distributed State Store | Encrypted control plane state read/write |
| Audit Events | Outbound | SecOps SIEM/Monitoring | Control plane audit log stream |
| Secrets Access | Outbound | GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-VAULT-2.7.21 | Retrieval of encryption keys for state-at-rest |
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SCP-2.7.16.md#zero-trust-alignment-nist-sp-800-207]

### Zero Trust Alignment (NIST SP 800-207)

Control Plane Security advances the Applications and Workloads pillar at its highest-impact layer — the control plane determines what runs and where, making it the highest-value target in the container platform. Protecting it directly supports the Zero Trust principle that infrastructure components must not be implicitly trusted.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SCP-2.7.16.md#nist-sp-800-53-intent-alignment]

### NIST SP 800-53 Intent Alignment

This ABB enables the architectural intent of the SC (System and Communications Protection) family — specifically protection of system management interfaces and inter-component communication — and the AU (Audit and Accountability) family, which requires tamper-evident audit records of privileged operations.
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SCP-2.7.16.md#constraints-and-dependencies]

### Constraints and Dependencies

- Control plane security architecture varies between managed Kubernetes services (where the cloud provider owns the control plane) and self-managed deployments; architecture decisions must account for the shared responsibility model.
- Key management for state encryption (GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-VAULT-2.7.21) must be available and resilient before control plane encryption is enabled.
- Audit log volume from the control plane can be substantial; forwarding architecture must be sized appropriately.
